snippet.title: True Size - French Army of the Hundred Years War (1337-1453) DOCUMENTARY
snippet.description:
Watch the full documentary on Joan of Arc (and more) with HistoryAdventures https://youtube.com/@HistoryAdventures-1?si=9Gnw0pkHq-MzyltD

In this history documentary we explore the True Size of the Army of Joan of Arc. This involves a review of the nature of the French Army as it entered the Hundred Years War. We cover its method of organization, equipment, and muster. The major phases of the war are then covered to highlight the changes to the military of medieval france. This includes casualties from battles like Crecy and Agincourt as well as the broader cullings of the Black Death. We then review the nature of the army of 1430 when Joan of Arc emerged to lead it. The documentary then covers the early campaigns of the maiden which culminates in the Siege of Orleans.

snippet.title: The Lombards - Germanics Conquered the Roman Heartland
snippet.description:
🎥 Watch 300+ exclusive videos on ✔ youtube ► https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCMmaBzfCCwZ2KqaBJjkj0fw/join and ✔ Patreon ► https://www.patreon.com/kingsandgenerals

Kings and Generals animated historical documentary series on the history of medieval period and Franks continues with a video on how the history of the Lombards. Before Lombardy became a region of Italy, the Lombards were a roaming warrior people whose origin story mixed myth, migration, politics, and war. This video follows their rise from the legendary “long-beards” of the Winnils to one of the most important Germanic kingdoms of the early Middle Ages. We trace how a small tribal coalition entered Roman records, settled in Pannonia, fought the Heruli and Gepids, and served the Eastern Roman Empire before turning against it. Under King Alboin, the Lombards invaded a devastated Italy in 568, seized Milan and Pavia, and carved out a kingdom among the ruins of Rome. But conquest brought instability: murder, autonomous dukes, Byzantine resistance, religious change, and a society built around warriors, law, honour, and hierarchy. The story then turns to the 8th century, when Lombard expansion threatened Rome itself, forcing the Pope to seek protection from the rising Carolingian Franks. From Alboin’s bloody legend to Pippin’s invasions and the birth of the Papal States, this is the story of how the Lombards reshaped Italy—and why their kingdom could not survive Frankish power. It is a transformation story linking Rome’s collapse, barbarian migration, medieval state-building, and the rise of Charlemagne’s world in medieval Europe.

snippet.title: The Roman Wedding Night Ritual So Brutal It Was Hidden for 2,000 Years
snippet.description:
"The Roman Wedding Night Ritual So Brutal It Was Hidden for 2,000 Years"

Every Roman bride's hair was parted with an actual spear on her wedding day — and that was only the beginning. This documentary uncovers the real, documented rituals behind ancient Roman weddings, verified through the writings of Plutarch, Livy, Catullus, Festus, and Ovid.
From the hasta caelibaris spear ritual, to the ceremonial "abduction" of 
the bride from her mother's arms, to the disturbing language ancient poets used to describe the wedding night itself — Roman marriage customs were built entirely around the performance of conquest, not consent.

This is the real history behind traditions that still echo in weddings 
today, including the veil, the wedding ring, and the phrase "tying the 
knot" — verified through primary Roman and Greek sources rather than 
legend or assumption.

"In the summer of 1546, one woman faced a punishment so brutal that it shocked even many of her contemporaries. Her name was Anne Askew, a young English noblewoman whose religious beliefs brought her into direct conflict with the authorities during the reign of Henry VIII.

Accused of heresy during one of the most turbulent periods of the English Reformation, Anne Askew endured imprisonment, interrogation, and torture in an attempt to force her to reveal the names of influential supporters. Despite immense pressure, she refused to abandon her convictions. Her courage ultimately led her to one of the most feared forms of execution in Tudor England—the stake.

This historical documentary explores the dramatic final months of Anne Askew’s life, the religious struggles that divided England, and the political intrigue surrounding the royal court. Discover how faith, power, and persecution collided in a kingdom undergoing profound transformation.

Learn about the brutal realities of heresy trials, the dangerous atmosphere of Tudor politics, and the extraordinary resilience of a woman whose story became one of the most powerful symbols of religious conviction in English history.

From the prisons of London to the execution grounds of Smithfield, this documentary uncovers the true story behind one of England’s most infamous executions and the lasting legacy of Anne Askew.

Watch until the end to discover why her final stand continues to fascinate historians nearly five centuries later.

snippet.title: "This Ancient Empire's Punishment for Kings Was Worse Than Death"
snippet.description:

"This Ancient Empire's Punishment for Kings Was Worse Than Death"


What did ancient Assyrian kings really do to the rulers they defeated? This full documentary uncovers the brutal, calculated system of terror used by the Neo-Assyrian Empire — verified through royal inscriptions, palace reliefs, and archaeological evidence that has survived for nearly 2,700 years.From King Ashurnasirpal II's flaying of rebels at Suru, to the beheading of King Teumman of Elam at the Battle of the Ulai River, to Sennacherib's total 
destruction of Babylon in 689 BC — this video explores how Assyrian kings used fear as a political weapon to control their empire.

What punishment could possibly be worse than death for a king? This 
documentary reveals the terrifying methods the Neo-Assyrian Empire used 
against the rulers who dared to rebel — verified through royal inscriptions, 
palace reliefs, and archaeological evidence that has survived for nearly 
2,700 years.

From King Ashurnasirpal II's flaying of rebels at Suru, to the humiliating 
beheading of King Teumman of Elam displayed at a royal feast, to Sennacherib's 
total destruction of Babylon — Assyrian kings didn't just kill their enemies. 
They designed punishments meant to break them completely, erase their legacy, 
and send a message to every ruler watching.

But the story takes an unexpected turn. Discover how some defeated kings, 
like Manasseh of Judah, survived through calculated Assyrian mercy — proving 
this empire's cruelty was never random, but a precise political weapon.

snippet.title: The Genius Design Behind Star Fort Defenses - Origins of the US Anthem
snippet.description:
🎥 Watch 300+ exclusive videos on ✔ youtube ► https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCMmaBzfCCwZ2KqaBJjkj0fw/join and ✔ Patreon ► https://www.patreon.com/kingsandgenerals

Kings and Generals animated historical documentary series on early modern warfare where we talk about the evolution of the Star Fort, the genius behind its design and Fort Mchenry. When cannon fire made medieval castles obsolete, European engineers answered with one of the most important military designs in history: the bastion fort. This video traces the rise of the low, angular “star fort,” from Renaissance Italy and the Trace Italienne to the great fortress systems of the Netherlands, Habsburg frontier, and Vauban’s France. We explain why tall walls failed, how angled bastions eliminated blind spots, and why siege warfare became a deadly contest of mathematics, trenches, artillery, and engineering. Then the story crosses the Atlantic to Baltimore, where Fort McHenry turned European fortress theory into American coastal defence. Built on Whetstone Point to guard Baltimore Harbor, its pentagonal bastions, dry moat, glacis, and heavy guns faced their defining test during the War of 1812. After burning Washington, the British fleet bombarded Fort McHenry for 25 hours, but the fort held, the flag still flew, and Francis Scott Key found the image that became The Star-Spangled Banner. From Italian city-states to the Chesapeake, this is the story of how star forts changed warfare—and how one American bastion became a national symbol of resistance, engineering, and survival under fire, remembered long after the guns fell silent in 1814 and beyond forever.

snippet.title: What Happened to the Daughters of Defeated Roman Generals Will SHOCK You
snippet.description:
What Happened to the Daughters of Defeated Roman Generals Will SHOCK You 

What really happened to the children of Rome's most powerful defeated generals? 
This documentary reveals the untold story of Cleopatra's daughter, Cleopatra Selene, and Pompey's daughter, Pompeia — verified through the works of Plutarch, Suetonius, and Cassius Dio.
After Mark Antony's defeat at the Battle of Actium in 31 BC, his children were paraded through Rome in Octavian's triumph. But instead of execution, they were raised in the household of Octavia — Antony's own Roman wife. Cleopatra Selene would go on to become a reigning queen of Mauretania, while her father's Roman daughters became ancestors of Roman emperors including Caligula, Claudius, and Nero.
This is the strange, documented truth about how Rome turned the daughters of its defeated enemies into queens, mothers of emperors, and the hidden architects of its imperial bloodline.

From the incompetent Roman Consuls who treated war like a vacation, to the strict discipline of Lucius Aemilius Paullus, and the hilarious diplomatic failures that started it all—this is the story of how Rome turned the Mediterranean into their private lake.
